title: Hydrologic Technicians
description: Collect and organize data concerning the distribution and circulation of ground and surface water, and data on its physical, chemical, and biological properties. Measure and report on flow rates and ground water levels, maintain field equipment, collect water samples, install and collect sampling equipment, and process samples for shipment to testing laboratories. May collect data on behalf of hydrologists, engineers, developers, government agencies, or agriculture.

tasks.text: Apply research findings to minimize the environmental impacts of pollution, waterborne diseases, erosion, or sedimentation.
Develop computer models for hydrologic predictions.
Write materials for research publications, such as maps, tables, and reports, to disseminate findings.
Analyze ecological data about the impact of pollution, erosion, floods, and other environmental problems on bodies of water.
Estimate the costs and benefits of municipal projects, such as hydroelectric power plants, irrigation systems, and wastewater treatment facilities.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Answer technical questions from hydrologists, policymakers, or other customers developing water conservation plans.
Provide real time data to emergency management and weather service personnel during flood events.
Assist in designing programs to ensure the proper sealing of abandoned wells.
Prepare, install, maintain, or repair equipment used for hydrologic study, such as water level recorders, stream flow gauges, and water analyzers.
Investigate complaints or conflicts related to the alteration of public waters by gathering information, recommending alternatives, or preparing legal documents.
Perform quality control checks on data to be used by hydrologists.
Investigate the properties, origins, or activities of glaciers, ice, snow, or permafrost.
Locate and deliver information or data as requested by customers, such as contractors, government entities, and members of the public.
Collect water and soil samples to test for physical, chemical, or biological properties, such as pH, oxygen level, temperature, and pollution.
Measure the properties of bodies of water, such as water levels, volume, and flow.
Write groundwater contamination reports on known, suspected, or potential hazardous waste sites.

skills.name: Geographic information system
skills.def: Software to capture, manage, analyze, or display geographically-referenced information. Examples: ESRI ArcGIS software, ESRI ArcInfo, ESRI ArcView, Geographic information system GIS software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access, State Soil Geographic STATSGO Database.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adobe Acrobat.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Microsoft Active Server Pages ASP.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
